response: HTTP/2 still has transport-level head-of-line blocking: a lost TCP packet can delay unrelated streams. HTTP/3 runs over QUIC, so loss on one stream does not stall the others. HTTP/3 can also improve connection setup and network handoffs. HTTP/2 remains a sensible choice where compatibility, tooling, or operational simplicity outweigh those benefits.

No. A shared namespace and cluster-admin service accounts turn a small mistake or compromised service into cluster-wide access. Use separate namespaces by environment or trust boundary, dedicated service accounts, and least-privilege RBAC. You can keep deployment simple without making authorization global.

RAID 1 protects against a drive failing. A backup protects against deleted files, corruption, ransomware, accidental changes, and loss of the machine or site. Mirroring a bad change mirrors the damage immediately. RAID is useful availability infrastructure; keep separate, versioned backups as well.

MongoDB is not the standard default for financial ledgers; systems needing strong transactional guarantees and auditability often use relational databases. MongoDB can still support a ledger if its constraints fit your workload. Model each journal entry as an immutable transaction containing balanced debit and credit postings, enforce that total debits equal total credits in a transaction, assign stable account and transaction IDs, and never update posted entries—create reversing entries instead.

Kafka does not delete a record when a consumer reads it. Records remain in a topic until the retention policy removes them, while each consumer group tracks its own offset. Put both services in separate consumer groups; each group will receive and process the same events independently.

Usually not. Finish a chapter or two, then get feedback from readers who match the book’s audience. Early feedback exposes problems with premise, structure, voice, and level of detail while changes are still cheap. Keep drafting, but validate the direction before committing to the entire manuscript.

The $200k matters for accounting and for understanding what happened, but it is already spent either way. The decision is whether the expected value of finishing exceeds the additional cost, time, and opportunity cost from today onward. Finish if the forward case is strong; stop if it is not.

Standups are not universally wasteful. They help when a team needs rapid coordination, but become wasteful when they are status theater or solve no active coordination problem. Replace them with an async written update plus a short, opt-in blocker discussion; keep a live standup only where dependencies and blockers genuinely require it.
